nice-recommends-enhertu-her2-low-breast-.name: NICE recommends Enhertu for HER2-low cancer
nice-recommends-enhertu-her2-low-breast-.summary: NICE said on 17 September 2026 that it recommends Enhertu for adults with HER2-low advanced breast cancer that has progressed after treatment, after a commercial solution was agreed.
keyPoints: NICE published the news on 17 September 2026 and recommends Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) for adults with HER2-low advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has progressed after treatment.
NICE says a commercial solution has now been agreed with the companies.
NICE's guidance page lists the final guidance, TA1197, as published on 7 October 2026.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
NICE says it recommends Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) for adults with HER2-low advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has progressed after treatment. HER2 is a protein found on the surface of some breast cancer cells, and HER2-low describes cancers with a low level of it.

The recommendation appears in NICE's final draft guidance. NICE's independent committee had earlier been unable to recommend the drug at the price the companies proposed.

NICE says a commercial solution has now been agreed. It followed changes to NICE's methods made as part of the UK/US Pharmaceutical Pricing Agreement.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
A final draft recommendation is a step before final guidance. NICE's guidance page for the appraisal, TA1197, lists final guidance as published on 7 October 2026 and says it replaces earlier guidance (TA992), which had not recommended the drug.

The announcement concerns people whose breast cancer is advanced and has progressed after treatment. Treatment decisions for an individual are made by their cancer team. The site's breast cancer page explains the condition and how it is usually diagnosed and treated.

source.title: NICE recommends Enhertu for people with HER2-low advanced breast cancer

ukhsa-flu-levels-low-but-higher-than-pre.name: UKHSA: flu low but above last four years
ukhsa-flu-levels-low-but-higher-than-pre.summary: UKHSA reported on 8 October 2026 that flu levels were low at the start of the season but higher than at the same point in the previous four years, and urged eligible people to be vaccinated.
keyPoints: UKHSA reported on 8 October 2026 that flu activity was low at the start of the season but higher than in each of the previous four years.
UKHSA described possible signs of an early flu season.
UKHSA says it takes a couple of weeks for the vaccine to give full protection.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
UKHSA says flu activity in September was higher than in the same period of each of the past four winters, although it remained at baseline, which means very low levels. Flu trends have been rising since August, and UKHSA says there are possible signs of an early flu season.

In a related UKHSA blog post, the agency says the rise so far has been driven largely by cases in 18 to 24 year olds. Early typing data show an equal mix of influenza A(H3N2) and A(H1N1) in England.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
UKHSA urges people who are eligible to be vaccinated. It says the vaccine takes a couple of weeks to give full protection, so getting it sooner rather than later is better.

The blog post also notes that last season started early but was milder overall, with lower activity and mortality than the year before. This site's influenza vaccine page explains the vaccine in more detail.

source.title: Flu levels low at start of season but higher than previous 4 years

references.title: Flu levels low at start of season but higher than previous 4 years

ukhsa-diwali-urges-flu-covid-rsv-vaccina.name: UKHSA urges vaccination before Diwali
ukhsa-diwali-urges-flu-covid-rsv-vaccina.summary: On 30 October 2026 UKHSA asked eligible people celebrating Diwali to get their flu, COVID-19 and RSV vaccines before the festivities, saying protection takes several days to build.
keyPoints: UKHSA published the message on 30 October 2026 for people celebrating Diwali who are eligible for flu, COVID-19 and RSV vaccines.
UKHSA says the vaccines can take several days to provide maximum protection.
UKHSA notes that children can have the free flu vaccine at school, or a nasal vaccine at a participating pharmacy.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
UKHSA is calling on eligible people who celebrate Diwali to come forward for flu, COVID-19 and RSV vaccines before the festival. It says the vaccines can take several days to give maximum protection, so earlier is better.

The agency also says indoor gatherings in enclosed spaces with less ventilation can help airborne viruses spread.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
UKHSA points out that eligible children can have the free flu vaccine at school, and that this year children can also have the nasal flu vaccine at a participating pharmacy. It adds that pregnant women and people aged 75 and over can have the RSV vaccine.

Eligibility depends on age and health, and the NHS decides who is invited. This site's influenza vaccine page describes the flu vaccine.

source.title: Don't let a winter bug ruin your Diwali celebrations

references.title: Don't let a winter bug ruin your Diwali celebrations

mhra-new-safeguards-antidepressant-safet.name: MHRA adds antidepressant safety safeguards
mhra-new-safeguards-antidepressant-safet.summary: On 15 October 2026 the MHRA announced new safeguards for antidepressant safety information after a review of 28 antidepressants, covering suicidal thoughts and behaviours and sexual dysfunction that continues after stopping.
keyPoints: The MHRA announced the measures on 15 October 2026 after a review by an expert working group of the Commission on Human Medicines.
The review looked at how two risks are communicated to patients for 28 antidepressant medicines.
The measures include a boxed warning in patient leaflets, a patient card and a new safety leaflet.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says an expert working group of the Commission on Human Medicines has finished a detailed review of how the potential risks of 28 antidepressant medicines are communicated to patients. The review began after concerns from patients and families about the information in patient information leaflets.

The two risks are suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and sexual dysfunction that continues after treatment is stopped.

body.heading: What changes
body.body:
The MHRA lists a new boxed warning in the leaflets, to highlight information on suicidal thoughts and behaviours and point to where help can be found. A new patient card, in digital or paper form, reinforces key safety messages. A new safety leaflet is being developed with other health system partners and can be given out by healthcare professionals. A public assessment report was published alongside the announcement.

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 999. For urgent mental health help, NHS 111 offers a mental health option, and Samaritans are free to call on 116 123 at any time. The site's SSRI, sertraline and citalopram pages cover this group of medicines.

source.title: MHRA introduces new safeguards to strengthen antidepressant safety information following major review

mhra-approves-lurbinectedin-small-cell-l.name: MHRA approves lurbinectedin for lung cancer
mhra-approves-lurbinectedin-small-cell-l.summary: The MHRA approved lurbinectedin (Zepzelca) on 23 September 2026 for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, as maintenance treatment with atezolizumab.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved lurbinectedin (Zepzelca) on 23 September 2026 for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
It is approved in combination with atezolizumab as maintenance treatment.
The MHRA says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of lurbinectedin under close review.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has approved lurbinectedin (Zepzelca) for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. It is approved in combination with atezolizumab as maintenance treatment, for adults whose cancer has not progressed after first-line induction treatment with atezolizumab, carboplatin and etoposide.

The approval came through the International Recognition Procedure (Route B), with the European Medicines Agency as the reference regulator. The MHRA describes a main study of 483 adults with extensive-stage disease.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA explains that lurbinectedin attaches to DNA inside cancer cells, which damages the DNA and disrupts cell growth and division, leading to cell death. The MHRA says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of the medicine under close review.

Approval by the MHRA is a licensing decision. It is separate from decisions on NHS funding. The site's lung cancer page explains the condition.

source.title: MHRA approves lurbinectedin for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer

references.title: MHRA approves lurbinectedin for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer

mhra-recall-xeal-pharma-clopidogrel-oral.name: MHRA recalls Xeal Pharma clopidogrel liquids
mhra-recall-xeal-pharma-clopidogrel-oral.summary: The MHRA issued a Class 2 recall on 26 October 2026 of all strengths of Xeal Pharma's clopidogrel oral liquids, which contain less than the labelled amount of clopidogrel.
keyPoints: The MHRA issued the Class 2 medicines recall (reference EL(26)A/43) on 26 October 2026.
Xeal Pharma told the MHRA that all strengths of its clopidogrel oral suspension and oral solution contain less than the labelled amount.
The notice says no reports of patient harm have been received.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA notice says Xeal Pharma has informed it that all strengths of its Clopidogrel Oral Suspension and Clopidogrel Oral Solution contain less than the labelled amount of clopidogrel. The notice attributes this to a formulation error. Affected batches contain 76% of the required amount, and the recall covers all batches produced before the notice.

Pharmacists and wholesalers are told to stop supplying the affected batches and to quarantine remaining stock.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
Based on Xeal Pharma's risk assessment, the notice says patient harm is not anticipated in patients receiving the product for long-term preventative treatment, and that no reports of patient harm have been received. It says patients may need a corrected dose, an alternative licensed formulation or a different treatment, and that no licensed clopidogrel oral suspension or solution is available.

Xeal Pharma has confirmed that future stock will be made with the correct strength. Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medicine, and the site has a page on it.

source.title: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Xeal Pharma, Clopidogrel Oral Liquids (all strengths), EL(26)A/43

references.title: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Xeal Pharma, Clopidogrel Oral Liquids (all strengths), EL(26)A/43

nhs-england-pharmacies-treat-migraines-a.name: NHS pharmacies to treat migraine and acne
nhs-england-pharmacies-treat-migraines-a.summary: NHS England announced on 10 September 2026 that, from autumn, pharmacies will treat migraines, acne and three other everyday conditions through a new prescribing service.
keyPoints: NHS England announced the plan on 10 September 2026.
The five conditions are acne, migraines, scabies, ear infections and rhinitis, and the service starts from autumn.
Coverage depends on which pharmacies apply to become prescribing pharmacies.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
NHS England says pharmacies in England will be able to treat five more everyday conditions from autumn without a GP appointment: acne, migraines, scabies, ear infections and seasonal allergic rhinitis. Qualified pharmacist prescribers in taking-part pharmacies will assess and treat them.

The migraine pathway is for adults with low-frequency episodic migraine. The acne pathway covers mild to moderate acne in young people and adults.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The service works through a new prescribing service. A pharmacy that employs a pharmacist with a prescribing qualification can apply to become a prescribing pharmacy, so availability will depend on which pharmacies sign up.

NHS England says pharmacies already support people with seven common conditions under Pharmacy First, which has delivered 14 million consultations since it began in February 2024. For migraine that is frequent or has other features, a GP appointment remains the route; the site's migraine page explains the condition.

source.title: Patients to get quicker treatment for migraines, acne and 3 other everyday conditions at pharmacies

references.title: Patients to get quicker treatment for migraines, acne and 3 other everyday conditions at pharmacies

dhsc-under-18-sales-ban-vapes-nicotine-p.name: Under-18 ban on vapes and nicotine in force
dhsc-under-18-sales-ban-vapes-nicotine-p.summary: New rules took effect on 29 October 2026 making it illegal to sell any vape or non-medicinal nicotine product to anyone under 18, according to a Department of Health and Social Care explainer.
keyPoints: The Department of Health and Social Care published its explainer on 29 October 2026, the day the rules took effect.
Selling any vaping product or non-medicinal nicotine product to under-18s is illegal, online or in shop.
Adults who buy these products for under-18s now commit an offence.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The Department of Health and Social Care says it is illegal to sell any vaping product or non-medicinal nicotine product to anyone under 18, whether online or in a shop. The ban now covers nicotine-free vapes, which were not covered before, and tobacco-free nicotine pouches. Medicinally licensed products fall under separate medicines law.

Buying these products for someone under 18, known as proxy purchasing, is now an offence.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The rules restrict free giveaways and substantial discounts used to promote sales and ban most vending-machine sales. Councils and Trading Standards can issue £200 fixed penalty notices. Legal vaping products remain available to adults.

The Chief Medical Officer is quoted as saying vaping is considered safer than smoking but that this is a low bar, and that vapes should never be used by children or non-smokers. Separate tobacco rules are due later: from 1 January 2027 it will be illegal to sell tobacco to anyone born on or after 1 January 2009. See the site's smoking page for health information.

source.publisher: Department of Health and Social Care
source.title: New vape and nicotine rules explained

references.title: New vape and nicotine rules explained
